column1: # The rename table. Tab-separated. Source of truth for tools/dev_env/rename_modules.py - edit here,
# old      the directory the module arrived in
# latin    the category name: directory, filename, include path, header guard, typedef prefix
# stem     the shortened Latin stem: namespace instance, and the default symbol infix
# pascal   the latin name in PascalCase, for the Ns / Vars / V / Ctx / Args typedefs
# The mmgr_<infix>_ prefix each symbol carries. Read out of the code, not assumed from the
# directory: protomem declares mmgr_mem_*, membuild declares mmgr_sb_*, bitio declares mmgr_bitw_*.
# An infix that NAMES ITS MODULE collapses to that module's stem. An infix that names a distinct
# CONCEPT inside the module keeps its own identity, because collapsing it would merge two things
# that are not the same thing. tools/dev_env checked this rather than assuming it: collapsing
# rawmemcpy's three onto one stem merged seven symbol pairs including the aligned and the unaligned
# load, and collapsing cspan onto span merged the const and non-const constructors.
# The three access strategies of proximus_operor. Not one thing under three names: raw is
# unaligned, al is aligned, mv may alias. Merging them is a miscompile the compiler cannot report.
# The const span. Long form in the declaration, f- for fixus in the symbol.
# Unchanged. dma and mpint and pingpong name concepts, not modules; worker is cross-cutting and is
# declared by confinium but used by the pools.
# alloc is out. capio takes, reddo gives back, interim replaces scratch entirely.
# free_bytes is NOT a release and does not become reddo: it returns a count of bytes still
# available. octas_praesto - "bytes at hand". persist_free DOES take a pointer, so it is a real
# The data typedefs keep the existing lowercase mmgr_ convention - they are the public C API types
# and the prefix is what namespaces them. They take the STEM rather than the long Latin, because the
# symbol pass already produced mmgr_confin_set, and a type spelled mmgr_confinium beside a function
# spelled mmgr_confin_set_add reads as two different modules.
# The namespace type is PascalCase and takes the FULL Latin name - it is the module's identity, it
# appears once per module, and nothing about it is repeated at a call site. The instance beside it
# is the stem, because that IS the call site: memor.cpy(work), not memoria_operor.cpy(work).
# The instance is rewritten ONLY at its declaration and at `<name>.` member access. Never as a bare
# identifier: `mem` is also a struct member holding the pool storage, `span` and `raw` are
# function-pointer member names inside these very structs, and `secure` appears inside an assert
# message. A bare-identifier rename corrupts all four.
